script: The CIA once built an exploding cigar with one target, killing a single man. Throughout the 1960s, American intelligence tried to assassinate Cuban leader Fidel Castro using an exhausting list of failed gadgets, poisoned cigars, an exploding seashell planted where he liked to dive, and chemicals meant to make his beard fall out to humiliate him publicly. Agents obsessed over Castro's exact habits for years, tailoring every device specifically to him. But here's the part nobody mentions, congressional investigators later found over six hundred separate assassination attempts on record, and not one of them ever came close to working. Castro outlived nearly every American president who tried to have him killed. The CIA spent years engineering a single man's death, and the exploding cigar never even reached his hands.

title: The CIA Tried Over 600 Times to Kill One Man. Not One Attempt Worked
description:
Throughout the 1960s, the CIA attempted to assassinate Fidel Castro with an exploding cigar, a poisoned wetsuit, and dozens of other bizarre gadgets. Congressional investigators later confirmed over 600 attempts on record, and none of them worked.

Which failed attempt sounds crazier to you, the cigar or the exploding seashell? CIGAR or SEASHELL. Say your pick below.
